completeness.reason: The mechanism covers the restore obligation, but the parent's numeric part - within 2 % of rated capacity of the last published value - is not engaged: after an unexpected power loss the surviving slot can be up to 60 s stale, and nothing bounds the charge that may have moved in that window against the 2 % budget.
completeness.suggestion: Justify the 60 s period against the 2 % bound, or make the periodic write charge-triggered (write whenever the accumulated charge since the last write corresponds to a stated fraction of rated capacity) so the worst-case restore error is bounded by design.

consistency.reason: No sibling shares REQ_SOC_PERSISTENCE, and the element does not contradict any related element - it hands the restored value to ARCH_OCV_CORRECTOR as a starting anchor, which is exactly what that element declares it owns.

design_clarity.reason: Names concrete choices: a two-slot alternating record with value, monotonic write counter and checksum, two explicit write triggers (every shutdown request plus every 60 s awake), and an unambiguous restore rule (highest-counter valid slot).

implementability.reason: Realisable and bounded, but an implementer must decide the cold-start behaviour when neither slot is valid (first-ever boot or both checksums bad) and must judge the NVM endurance implications of a 60 s write cadence over vehicle life.
implementability.suggestion: State what is handed to the corrector when no valid slot exists, and name the storage medium/endurance assumption that makes a 60 s write cadence acceptable.

parent_fit.reason: Substantively addresses REQ_SOC_PERSISTENCE: it owns the non-volatile shadow of the published SoC, writes it around shutdown, and hands the surviving slot back as the wake-up anchor so the first post-power-cycle publication continues from the pre-shutdown value.

summary: A well-chosen persistence mechanism - two alternating slots, monotonic counter, checksum, and a stated slot-selection rule. What is missing is the link between the 60 s periodic write and the parent's 2 % bound: charge moved between the last periodic write and an unexpected power loss is unaccounted for.
